site.tagline: Squad tactics in a browser tab.
site.description: Command a platoon of up to twelve tanks. Pick the ground, freeze time to plan every route, then radio your squad through a live firefight. No install, no account.

page.lead: Command a platoon of up to twelve tanks on a grid built from real page elements. Pick the ground, freeze time to plan every route, then radio your squad through a live firefight. Free in your browser: no install, no account.

poster.alt: DOM Battlefield mid-battle: the green platoon pushes across the grid toward HQ B while pink tanks hold the cover, with the sector map in the corner

howToPlay.title: Pick the ground
howToPlay.body: Choose one of four operations, a terrain density and your side, or press Quick start and anything you have not picked is rolled at random.

howToPlay.title: Plan the battle
howToPlay.body: Time is frozen. Set your formation and a squad of 4, 8 or 12 tanks. Fill a four-slot scout, medium and heavy loadout within 12 points, then give each tank an order.

howToPlay.title: Fight
howToPlay.body: Press Start battle. Drive your command tank with WASD or the arrows, aim with the pointer and hold Space or click to fire. Your command tank must survive.

howToPlay.title: Command under fire
howToPlay.body: Press O for Command mode: time runs at half speed and your gun is off while you send tanks to new squares. F, R and E order fall in, retreat and advance.

howToPlay.title: Win
howToPlay.body: Capture the enemy HQ, hold the contested crossroads, or eliminate their platoon.

controls.title: Drive
controls.body: WASD or the arrow keys. On phones, the analog thumbstick.

controls.title: Aim and fire
controls.body: Aim with the pointer; hold Space, click or right-click to fire. On phones, aim goes to the nearest visible enemy: hold Fire.

controls.title: Squad orders
controls.body: F fall in, R retreat, E advance. On phones, the labeled buttons.

controls.title: Pick a wingman
controls.body: 1–9 or click a tank. On phones, tap the tank or its platoon key.

controls.title: Command mode
controls.body: O, then a tank and a square. Enter locks the order, Backspace clears it, N moves to the next tank and H attacks the HQ.

controls.title: Pause and camera
controls.body: P or the white flag pauses: Keep fighting or Surrender. M and drag pans, C recenters.

modes.title: Quick start
modes.body: Anything you have not picked is rolled at random, and the battle starts.

modes.title: Plan battle
modes.body: Time stays frozen while three cards set your platoon, your loadout and every tank's route. Start battle when you are ready.

modes.title: Four operations
modes.body: Hedgerow breach, Desert spearhead, Winter crossroads and Twin bridges, each with Light, Normal or Heavy terrain and a dice for a new layout.

modes.title: Three ways to win
modes.body: Capture an opposing HQ, hold a contested crossroads, or eliminate a platoon.

tips.title: Retreat to repair
tips.body: Retreat sends your squad back to headquarters, where tanks repair. Advance returns them to the objective.

tips.title: Bend the route
tips.body: Drag a route line or its flag to change where a tank goes. Every map has alternate connected routes.

tips.title: Know your cover
tips.body: Houses, hedges and parked cars break into debris and rubble. Rocks and water are permanent; fences stop tanks but let shells through.

tips.title: True full screen on phones
tips.body: On iPhone, Add to Home Screen; on Android, Install. The first visit on a phone explains how.

items.title: Same battles
items.body: DOM Battlefield now runs on the Fizlet engine. Gameplay is unchanged: the new step plays the 0.18.13 battles identically.

items.title: Same seed, same battle
items.body: Every random roll in play comes from the map's seed, so a map replays the same way from the same inputs.

items.title: No garbage-collection hitches
items.body: Once warm, a battle step allocates nothing (tested: no minor GC over 20,000 busy steps).

faq.q: Is DOM Battlefield free to play?
faq.a: Yes. It plays in your browser with no install and no account, and it is open source (MIT).

faq.q: Can I play DOM Battlefield on a phone?
faq.a: Yes. Phone battles put a see-through rail on each side of a full-screen field, with an analog thumbstick and labeled buttons.

faq.q: How is it related to Sherman Bytes?
faq.a: Same tanks: Sherman Bytes draws every tank with its own sprite code. DOM Battlefield adds zero bytes to the Sherman game.
Not in DOM Battlefield yet. Battlefield Blitz, its arcade version, has a two-player mode.
